info.title: Ludus Engine API
info.description: Backend engine for 2D games. Content is authored in the editor and served to game clients over the public routes, which are cacheable and validated by ETag.

get.description: Empty when the project has not defined one; a player then has no stage.

put.description: Wholesale. The stages are only meaningful relative to each other, so editing one in isolation can leave a stage that begins before the one before it. Every problem is reported at once, with the index.

get.summary: Fetch a wave's document, draft or not
get.description: Returns the stored bytes exactly as they were received.

put.description: The id in the URL and the id in the document must agree.
The wave list is replaced wholesale, in the order given.

delete.description: The waves themselves are untouched; only their membership of this level goes. Deleting the active level leaves the project with none active.

put.description: `descending` says whether a bigger number is better. It belongs to the board rather than to a query, so two callers cannot disagree about a player's rank.

delete.description: Its scores go with it, by foreign key.

put.description: Attributes are validated against this project's own item schema, if it has declared one. Violations are reported at /attributes plus the pointer inside the document.

delete.description: It is removed from every player's inventory too, by foreign key.

get.description: An empty object when the project has not declared one, which validates nothing.

put.description: Refused now rather than on first use if it is unusable. Remote $ref targets are rejected: the engine will not fetch a URL chosen by whoever wrote the schema. Existing items are not re-validated.

get.description: An empty object when the project has never been configured.

put.description: The whole document, not a patch. The engine does not interpret any of these keys, so it has no basis for merging one document into another.

post.summary: Several published documents at once
post.description: For a first launch, when a client has nothing cached. Unknown or unpublished ids are simply absent. Not cacheable; revalidate with the single document routes.

post.summary: Exchange the game's player identifier for a session token
post.description: Creates the player on first sight, and is idempotent: retrying after a network failure resolves the same player rather than making a second one. Requires an API key. The token it returns is the only credential that can write this player's state, and only this player's.

post.summary: Spend from this player's balance
post.description: Refused with a 422 when the balance is insufficient, rather than clamped to zero. A player can spend their own currency; only an editor can award it.

get.summary: Where this player sits on a board
get.description: 404 when they have not scored on it.

post.summary: Record this player's score
post.description: The better of the new score and the existing one is kept, in the board's own direction. Always this player: there is no route that writes another's.

post.summary: Exchange an email address and password for tokens
post.description: Every failure returns the same 401 with the same body. The difference between an unknown address and a wrong password is not something to tell whoever is asking.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new pair
post.description: The presented token is revoked as part of the exchange, so a stolen token and the real one cannot both keep working.

post.summary: Create a wave from a document
post.description: The document's own id is used. Saving never publishes: a new wave is a draft and invisible to clients until it is published.

post.summary: Withdraw a wave. Clients stop seeing it entirely, as a 404.
Publish a wave, making it visible to clients
Create or replace many waves at once
post.description: All or nothing: one invalid document rejects the whole batch, and every violation is reported with the index of the document that caused it. Imported waves are drafts, like any other save.

post.summary: Delete many waves at once
post.description: All or nothing. An id that is not there is a violation rather than a silent skip: 'delete these six' is a statement about a known set.

post.summary: Create a level
post.description: The waves are listed in play order. Creating a level never activates it; activation is a separate call.

post.summary: Make this the level players receive
post.description: Replaces whatever was active. A project has at most one active level, which the database guarantees rather than this endpoint.

post.summary: Upload item art
post.description: PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF. SVG is refused deliberately: it can carry script, and it would run on this engine's origin.

post.summary: Award currency to a player
post.description: Editors and above. Not available to a game client: an API key ships inside the binary, so a client-authorised grant makes the currency whatever a modified binary says it is.

post.summary: Award several currencies and XP together
post.description: All or nothing: one rejected grant rolls back the whole reward.

post.summary: Give or take several items at once
post.description: All or nothing: one rejected line rolls back the whole grant. A player who received the sword and not the shield has been given something the game never offered.

get.summary: List audio clips. Metadata only; no file is opened.

post.summary: Upload an audio clip
post.description: Streamed to storage; the recorded size is what was actually written, not a length the client declared.

post.summary: Mix several clips into one
post.description: The result is an ordinary clip afterwards: served, listed and deleted like any upload. Returns 503 when this engine has no mixer configured.

post.summary: Mint a key. The response is the only time it is shown.

get.summary: The player this token acts as
get.description: There is no route for another player's profile, deliberately.

patch.summary: Set or clear this player's display name
patch.description: Blank clears it. Names are not unique; two players may share one.

get.summary: Every published wave, in progression order
get.description: Summaries only. Fetch a document from the raw route when you need it.

404.description: No such published wave. A draft answers this way too

get.description: Byte-for-byte what was stored. Cache these bytes with the ETag.
Published waves only, in play order. 404 when the project has no active level.

200.description: The active level and its published waves

404.description: This project has no active level

get.summary: The content hash for everything published
get.description: Compare it with the one you cached. Unchanged means play from cache and make no further requests. This value is identical to the ETag of the wave list for the same data.
Cached immutably: a sprite never changes under its id.
Cached immutably: a clip never changes under its id, so a client that has it never asks again.

get.summary: The settings this game should launch with
get.description: Byte-for-byte what was stored. Cache it with the ETag.
Read-only. Awarding currency needs a credential that does not ship in the game.
The stage is derived from the project's curve, not stored.
Read-only. Granting items needs a credential that does not ship in the game.

get.summary: A page of a board, in rank order
get.description: Cursor-paged. A row whose score does not change is returned exactly once across a walk, however many other scores are written meanwhile; a row whose score does change may move. There is no page number, deliberately.

get.summary: The identity behind the credential you presented
An order that would not collide
get.description: Advisory. The order lives in the document and the author owns it; this only answers what is free right now.
Cursor-paged: pass the nextCursor from the previous page. Offsets are not offered, because the ordering column changes on every session.

delete.description: Items referring to it are not changed. spriteRef is an opaque reference the game resolves -- it may be a URL or an atlas key -- so the engine has no list of what points at what.

delete.summary: Delete a clip and its bytes

delete.description: The row is kept and stamped, not deleted: when a key stopped working is a question people ask after an incident.

XpCurve.description: The project's XP curve, in ascending order.

XpStageView.description: One step of the project's XP curve.

WaveSummary.description: A wave's indexed fields. The document itself is fetched separately.

WaveLevelRequest.description: A level's name and the waves it sequences, in play order.

WaveLevelMember.description: One wave's place in a level, and whether players will receive it.

WaveLevelSummary.description: A level, its waves, and which of them players can actually reach.

LeaderboardRequest.description: A board to create or replace.

LeaderboardView.description: A board the project defines, and which way it sorts.

ItemRequest.description: An item to create or replace.

ItemView.description: An item the project defines. Attributes are the project's own shape.

PlayerSessionRequest.description: The game's own identifier for this player.

PlayerSession.description: A player session token and who it acts as.

PlayerSpendRequest.description: How much of which currency to spend.

PlayerBalance.description: How much of one currency a player has.

ScoreSubmission.description: A score to record. The better of the two is kept.

LeaderboardEntryView.description: One player's place. Rank is computed, not stored.

TokenResponse.description: A pair of tokens. The refresh token is shown once and is not recoverable.

SpriteSummary.description: An uploaded image. The bytes come from the public route.

PlayerGrantRequest.description: How much of which currency to award.

PlayerRewardRequest.description: Currencies and XP to award together, or not at all.

InventoryGrantRequest.description: Several items to grant together, or not at all.

ItemGrantRequest.description: An item and how many; negative takes them away.

InventoryEntryView.description: How many of one item a player holds.

AudioClipSummary.description: An audio clip's metadata. The bytes are fetched from the stream route.

AudioMixRequest.description: The clips to combine, and how loud each should be.

AudioMixTrack.description: One clip in a mix. Gain is in decibels; 0 leaves it alone.

name.description: So a human can tell keys apart

ApiKeyCreated.description: The only response that ever contains the key itself. It is stored as a digest, so it cannot be shown again by anyone, including whoever runs the database.

PlayerRenameRequest.description: A display name the player chose. Blank clears it.

PlayerProfile.description: A player's identity and when they were last seen.

PlayableWaveLevel.description: The level currently being played, and its published waves in order.

PlayerProgress.description: XP, the stage reached, and the next one.

LeaderboardPage.description: A page of a board, with the cursor for the next.

PlayerPage.description: Players, most recently seen first, with a cursor.
